summary: Seven open PRs and six open issues. Two issues (#3, #4) ask for the same opt-in fragment-free bookmark identity, and two open PRs (#9, #10) implement that identity with byte-equivalent behavior and identical tests — one should be consolidated. PRs #11 and #12 are complementary, not duplicates: #12 is Git-stacked on feat/csv-library and only adds CLI wiring, so #11 must be reviewed and merged first. Issue #8 (:443 duplication) is covered by the normalizer source currently on main, which strips default HTTP/HTTPS ports; this is the one case where attached current-main source, not merged history alone, supports an already-fixed finding. Issue #3 is only partially addressed by #9/#10 — current main's export_json and __main__ never pass strip_fragment, so the issue's "normalizer, export and CLI should agree" requirement is unmet. Issue #7 (query-parameter preservation coverage) has no open PR at all. PRs #26/#27 are labelled intentional contribution-review fixtures and are treated as demo controls, not accidental duplicates, even though #27's export_csv is identical to #11's. All actions are proposed only; nothing has been applied, and no rebase of any branch is recommended.

actions.rationale: Both issues describe the same defect and the same requested remedy: links differing only after '#' produce separate entries, and both ask for an opt-in document-level identity that leaves current defaults unchanged. #3 states the broader contract (shared normalizer, export and CLI must agree), so it is the better survivor; #4 contributes an extra reproduction. Proposed as consolidation under #3, not as a silent close of #4.

issues/4 body: 'Saving https://example.com/guide#a and https://example.com/guide#b produces two entries. Need an optional way to save one document entry rather than each section. Existing defaults must stay compatible.'
Both issues were opened by gvago within 2 seconds (2026-10-11T10:47:59Z and 10:48:01Z) and carry no labels, assignees or comments.

actions.draft: Thanks for both reports — these describe the same behavior: saved links that differ only after the '#' are kept as separate bookmarks, and both ask for an opt-in document-level identity that preserves today's defaults. I'd like to track the work on #3 since it spells out that the normalizer, the exporter and the CLI all have to agree, and keep this reproduction linked as extra context rather than losing it. If you think there's a requirement here that #3 doesn't cover, say so and we'll keep both open.

actions.rationale: These are duplicate implementations, confirmed by diff comparison rather than by title or shared filename. Both change the same two files, add the identical keyword-only parameter 'strip_fragment: bool = False' to normalize_url, produce the same output for every input, and add a test named test_optional_fragment_identity with character-identical assertions. The only difference is expression style: #9 inlines '"" if strip_fragment else parts.fragment' in the urlunsplit call, #10 assigns a local 'fragment' variable first. Both branch from the same base commit e565ba0. One should be chosen; the other closed with credit, not force-pushed or rebased.

actions.draft: #9 and #10 implement the same change: the same keyword-only `strip_fragment=False` parameter on `normalize_url`, the same default-preserving behavior, and the same `test_optional_fragment_identity` assertions. The only difference is whether the empty fragment is inlined in the `urlunsplit` call or assigned to a local first — no behavioral difference. I'd suggest we land one (I'd lean to #9 as the earlier submission) and close the other with credit in the merged PR description. Note that whichever lands, it only covers the helper — see the follow-up on #3 about exporter and CLI wiring.

actions.rationale: This finding rests on current-main source attached in the evidence, not on merged history alone. current_main bookmarks/urls.py (resolved_ref main, sha 13d048b, fetched 2026-10-11T16:48:32Z) contains the guard 'if port is not None and (parts.scheme, port) not in {("http", 80), ("https", 443)}: authority += f":{port}"', so https://example.com:443/docs and https://example.com/docs both normalize to https://example.com/docs. current_main bookmarks/exports.py routes every URL through normalize_url before dict.fromkeys dedup, so the export path inherits the fix. Merged PR #2 is corroborating history, not the basis of the claim. Proposed as a close-with-verification: the maintainer should run the two URLs on main before closing, because this is a source read, not an executed behavior check.

actions.rationale: Partial fix. Issue #3 requires that 'shared normalizer, export and CLI should agree', but both candidate PRs stop at the normalizer. Neither diff touches bookmarks/exports.py or bookmarks/__main__.py, and current main shows export_json calls normalize_url(url) with no strip_fragment argument and __main__ exposes no corresponding flag — so after merging either PR, a user exporting #intro and #install still gets two entries. The tests added are helper-level only. #3 should stay open after the merge, with exporter/CLI wiring and an end-to-end dedup regression tracked as follow-up.

actions.rationale: Intentional contribution-review fixtures, not accidental duplication. Both PR bodies say 'Contribution-review experiment; keep unmerged', they share base commit b27d830 and were opened five seconds apart on paired branches named -bad and -control. Importantly, #27's export_csv is byte-identical to #11's export_csv including the same test — under a pure diff comparison that would read as a duplicate PR of #11, but the branch naming and the explicit 'keep unmerged' note mark it as a deliberate control. These two should be excluded from duplicate-closure and merge recommendations. Separately, #26 is the intended negative case: it adds a third-party 'tabulate' dependency, bypasses normalize_url entirely (it calls url.lower() on raw input), and adds no test — all consistent with its role as the bad sample, not findings to act on.
